accessibility:
- **A modal dialog:** the viewer is a `Modal` with `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal`, named by
  `ariaLabel` ("Image viewer" by default) rather than by the image's alt, which changes with every
  image. Focus moves to the close button when it opens, Tab stays inside, Escape closes it when
  it's the topmost overlay, and focus goes back to the trigger, or to whatever had it when `open`
  was set.
- **Real triggers:** each `Lightbox.Trigger` is a `<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">`,
  or the button `Button` renders with `as={Button}`, named by its content. So the thumbnail's `alt`
  is the button's name, as long as it isn't inside a `<figure>` (give a ratio `Image` `as="div"`).
- **Every image has an alt:** `alt` is required in the type, a development build warns once for an
  item without one, and the caption is the `<figure>`'s `<figcaption>`, which names it.
- **Moves are announced:** after the viewer opens and after each move, a polite status line says
  "Image 3 of 10: Harbour at dusk", from `labels.progress` and the image's alt. The visible counter
  is hidden from screen readers, so it isn't read twice. For an image that fails to load, the line
  starts with `labels.loadError`: "This image didn't load. Image 3 of 10: Harbour at dusk", and a
  Retry that fails again is announced again.
- **At the ends:** with `repeat={false}`, the previous or next button is `aria-disabled` but stays in
  the tab order, so focus isn't dropped when it stops working. The zoom buttons do the same at their
  limits.
- **Single-pointer alternatives:** pinch has the zoom buttons and a double click or tap. Panning a
  zoomed image is a drag, so zoom-out and reset are always one press away, and the arrow keys pan.
- **Right to left:** the arrows, the keys and swipes follow the reading direction, so the next
  image is always the way the next arrow points.
- **Contrast:** the counter, the caption and the buttons' icons are white on Bulma's near-black
  modal background in both schemes, well over the 4.5:1 WCAG asks of text.
- **Forced colors:** the buttons draw their borders in the system's colors and the focus ring
  shows.
- **Motion:** the open fade, the crossfade between images and the zoom transition stop under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
summary: The `Lightbox` component shows a set of images one at a time in a modal viewer, with previous and next, a counter, captions and zoom, opened from the `Lightbox.Trigger` buttons you place. It renders its children where it stands, with no wrapper, and the viewer only while it's open, into a portal by default. The viewer is a `Modal`: focus moves to its close button, Tab stays inside, Escape and a click on the background close it, and focus goes back to the trigger.

parts.summary: The `Lightbox` component shows a set of images one at a time in a modal viewer, with previous and next, a counter, captions and zoom, opened from the `Lightbox.Trigger` buttons you place. It renders its children where it stands, with no wrapper, and the viewer only while it's open, into a portal by default. The viewer is a `Modal`: focus moves to its close button, Tab stays inside, Escape and a click on the background close it, and focus goes back to the trigger.

props.name: items
props.description: **Required.** The images, in order.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered in place: usually `Lightbox.Trigger`s, in whatever layout you like.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the viewer is open (controlled). With no `items` it shows nothing.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the viewer starts open (uncontrolled).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when a trigger, the close button, Escape, a click on the background or a swipe down opens or closes the viewer, and with `false` when `items` goes from some to none while it's open.

props.name: value
props.description: The index of the image shown (controlled). A value past either end is shown as the last or the first image, or wrapped round with `repeat`, without calling `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The image an uncontrolled viewer shows when something other than a trigger opens it. A trigger opens at its own `index`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new index when an arrow, a key or a swipe changes the image, and when a trigger opens the viewer, with the trigger's `index` even when that's the image already shown, before `onOpenChange(true)`. A parent that opens the viewer from `value` hears the trigger that way.

props.name: repeat
props.description: Go from the last image to the first and back, as Carousel does. Off, the previous and next buttons are `aria-disabled` at the ends.

props.name: zoomable
props.description: Zoom with the buttons, the wheel, a double click or tap, pinch and the `+`, `-` and `0` keys, and pan a zoomed image by dragging or with the arrow keys. Zoom waits for the image to load. `false` drops the zoom buttons and all of it.

props.name: maxZoom
props.description: How far an image zooms, as a multiple of its fitted size. The smallest zoom is always the fitted size.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Close on Escape. Only the topmost open overlay answers, as with Modal.

props.name: closeOnClickOutside
props.description: Close on a click on the dark background around the image. The space around the image, beside the toolbar's buttons and under the caption is all background.

props.name: portal
props.description: Renders the viewer into a portal: `true` for the `ConfigProvider`'s `portalContainer` (`document.body` by default), a selector string, or an element. `false` renders it in place. It's on by default, unlike Modal's, Dialog's and Command.Dialog's, because its triggers sit in gallery cells, and a cell with a transform or a filter would trap a viewer rendered in place.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: The dialog's accessible name. It stays the same from image to image; the status line says which image is shown.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it writes, for another language.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the viewer's `.modal` element, `null` while it's closed.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: A button around a thumbnail, or a line of text, that opens the viewer at its `index`.

props.name: as
props.description: Renders the trigger through another component, which gets its class, `aria-haspopup`, `type="button"`, click handler and ref along with its own props. `as={Button} color="link"` draws it as Bulma's link button.

props.name: index
props.description: **Required.** The index in `items` the viewer opens at.

props.name: children
props.description: What the button shows: a thumbnail, or text such as "View all photos". A ratio `Image` here takes `as="div"`, since its `<figure>` would keep the image's alt from naming the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders: the `<button>`, or what `Button` renders.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element or component selected by as (default <button>) and Bulma helper props
